name: Turkey
genZNote: Turkey (officially Türkiye) is the one country genuinely on two continents at once — Istanbul literally straddles Europe and Asia across the Bosphorus Strait, which is why it's every geography exam's favourite 'transcontinental country' example.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: A transcontinental country with territory in both Southeast Europe (East Thrace) and West Asia (Anatolia), separated by the Bosphorus Strait, Sea of Marmara, and Dardanelles.
Istanbul, its largest city, is the world's most notable example of a city spanning two continents.
Diverse terrain including the Anatolian plateau, extensive coastlines on the Mediterranean, Aegean, and Black Seas, and mountainous eastern regions.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Turkish is the official language; the culture blends Central Asian Turkic heritage, Islamic tradition, and centuries of Ottoman and Byzantine influence.
Predominantly Muslim, with a constitutionally secular state framework established by modern Turkey's founder, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk.
Rich culinary and artistic traditions, including Turkish cuisine, carpet weaving, and Ottoman-era architecture (e.g., the Hagia Sophia, Blue Mosque).

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A presidential republic; the modern secular republic was founded in 1923 by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk after the collapse of the Ottoman Empire.
Shifted from a parliamentary to an executive presidential system following a 2017 constitutional referendum.
Straddles the geopolitical space between Europe and the Islamic world, historically a candidate for European Union membership since 1987, though accession talks have long stalled.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A significant regional hub for medical tourism, particularly hair transplants, dental care, and cosmetic surgery.
Growing domestic defence industry, including drone technology (Bayraktar) that has drawn significant international attention.
Strong textile, automotive, and construction engineering sectors supporting a diversified industrial base.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A NATO member since 1952, occupying a strategically critical position bridging Europe, Asia, and the Middle East.
A long-standing EU candidate country, though full membership negotiations have stalled for decades over various political and human rights concerns.
Plays an active regional role in Middle Eastern, Caucasus, and Central Asian affairs, including involvement in Syria and support for Azerbaijan.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India-Turkey relations have historically been complex, shaped in part by Turkey's vocal diplomatic support for Pakistan's position on Kashmir at international forums.
Despite political friction, trade and commercial ties between the two countries have continued to grow, including in construction, textiles, and defence-adjacent sectors.
India sent significant humanitarian and disaster-relief assistance to Turkey following the devastating 2023 earthquakes, reflecting people-to-people goodwill despite governmental friction.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A large, diversified emerging economy strong in textiles, automotive manufacturing, construction, and increasingly defence technology (drones).
A major global tourism destination, leveraging its historical and coastal attractions.
Strategically positioned as a transit hub for energy pipelines connecting Central Asia and the Middle East to Europe.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being the world's most notable transcontinental country, spanning Europe and Asia.
Istanbul's Hagia Sophia and Ottoman-era architectural heritage.
A long-standing NATO member and EU candidate country.
Its rapidly growing domestic defence drone industry (Bayraktar).

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Turkey (Türkiye) is a transcontinental presidential republic spanning Europe and Asia, a NATO member and long-standing EU candidate rooted in Ottoman and Atatürk-era secular republican history.
keyFacts: Capital: Ankara (not Istanbul). Currency: Turkish Lira.
Presidential republic since a 2017 constitutional shift from a parliamentary system.
Modern secular republic founded in 1923 by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk.
NATO member since 1952; long-standing EU candidate country.
commonConfusion: Turkey's capital is Ankara, NOT Istanbul — Istanbul is the largest city and historic Ottoman capital, but Ankara has been the political capital since 1923.

highYieldFacts: Turkey: transcontinental country (Europe + Asia); capital Ankara, not Istanbul.
NATO member since 1952; long-standing EU candidate country.
India-Turkey: relations complicated by Turkey's support for Pakistan on Kashmir at international forums, despite growing trade ties.
commonTraps: Assuming Istanbul is Turkey's capital — it is Ankara.
Overlooking Turkey's shift from a parliamentary to a presidential system after the 2017 referendum.
mustRemember: Turkey: transcontinental NATO/EU-candidate republic, capital Ankara, complex India ties over Kashmir diplomacy.
